scientific_claim: INT8 PTQ preserves predictive accuracy and recall within +-0.5 percentage points.
calculation_or_experiment: Full test set evaluation (N=8,325): FP32 Acc 96.83%, PTQ Acc 96.95% (+0.12 pp); FP32 Recall 94.37%, PTQ Recall 94.10% (-0.27 pp).
limitations_and_caveats: Minority recall drops by 0.27 pp (1 flow misclassified: 351 vs 352 TP), well within +-0.5 pp parity threshold.
final_wording_recommendation: Maintain claim for PTQ: Post-training quantization preserves predictive performance within +-0.5 percentage points on both accuracy and minority recall.

scientific_claim: INT8 QAT maintains predictive parity within +-0.5 percentage points across all metrics.
calculation_or_experiment: Full test set evaluation (N=8,325): QAT Acc 97.37% (+0.54 pp vs FP32); QAT Recall 92.76% (-1.61 pp vs FP32); QAT Precision 64.31% (+5.15 pp vs FP32).
limitations_and_caveats: QAT violates the +-0.5 pp parity threshold: accuracy rises by +0.54 pp, but minority VPN recall drops by -1.61 pp (trades recall for precision).
final_wording_recommendation: Correct claim: QAT does not maintain strict +-0.5 pp parity across all metrics; it improves overall accuracy (+0.54 pp) and precision (+5.15 pp) while incurring a 1.61 pp drop in minority VPN recall.

scientific_claim: Model compression reduces deployment footprint by 10.5x.
calculation_or_experiment: FP32 training checkpoint (541.3 KB) vs INT8 PTQ state dict (51.6 KB) = 10.49x; FP32 state dict (182.7 KB) vs INT8 state dict (51.6 KB) = 3.54x; TorchScript (206.3 KB vs 84.8 KB) = 2.43x.
limitations_and_caveats: The 10.5x ratio compares a training checkpoint containing AdamW optimizer states against a deployment state dict.
final_wording_recommendation: Explicitly disaggregate: Deployment weight compression is 3.54x (approaching the theoretical 4.0x integer limit); 10.5x reduction applies specifically when comparing against full training checkpoints with optimizer buffers.

scientific_claim: Quantization accelerates CPU inference to 0.231 ms per flow (4,326 flows/s).
source_artifact: Benchmark evaluation across eager and TorchScript modes
calculation_or_experiment: At batch size 1: FP32 Eager = 0.094 ms, FP32 TorchScript = 0.054 ms, INT8 Eager = 0.197 ms, INT8 TorchScript = 0.038 ms. At batch size 32: FP32 Eager = 0.287 ms/flow, INT8 TorchScript = 0.020 ms/flow.
limitations_and_caveats: Eager INT8 is slower than eager FP32 at batch size 1 due to Python operator dispatch overhead. The speedup requires TorchScript compilation.
final_wording_recommendation: Attribute CPU latency acceleration to TorchScript compilation combined with INT8 SIMD vectorization, noting that eager quantized execution incurs dispatch overhead.

scientific_claim: INT8 PTQ induces severe attribution drift on VPN flows (Top-5 IoU collapses to 0.328, Spearman rho to 0.361).
calculation_or_experiment: KernelSHAP evaluation on 746 balanced flows: Non-VPN Top-5 IoU = 0.7839, rho = 0.7582. VPN Top-5 IoU = 0.3281, rho = 0.3610 (Mann-Whitney p = 3.43e-55).
limitations_and_caveats: Observed on flow-level stratified split using 150 perturbation samples per flow.
final_wording_recommendation: Maintain core finding: Despite predictive fidelity, INT8 PTQ induces severe feature attribution drift on complex VPN traffic.

scientific_claim: Attribution drift compounds causally across sequential convolutions as flow length increases.
source_artifact: Regression analysis on sample_level_metrics in attribution_drift_report.json
calculation_or_experiment: Linear regression: Top-5 IoU ~ active packets yields R^2 = 0.6230, slope = -0.0145, p = 9.44e-160. Within VPN: R^2 = 0.5369. Within Non-VPN: R^2 = 0.4994.
limitations_and_caveats: Strong empirical association confirmed, but combinatorial pool expansion also deflates chance IoU from 0.4707 (L=4) to 0.0220 (L=64). Layer-by-layer compounding is not directly isolated.
final_wording_recommendation: Report the strong empirical association (R^2 = 0.623) while framing causal compounding across conv layers as a mechanistic hypothesis to be isolated in future layer-ablation experiments.

scientific_claim: KernelSHAP seed variance is negligible, ruling out explainer sampling noise.
calculation_or_experiment: 5 seeds evaluated on 20 benchmark flows: mean pairwise Spearman rho = 0.5721 +- 0.3970, Top-5 IoU = 0.5359 +- 0.4025.
limitations_and_caveats: The data shows substantial sampling jitter (std = 0.3970). Sampling 150 permutations in a 128-dimensional continuous space inherently possesses stochasticity.
final_wording_recommendation: Correct claim: Acknowledge that KernelSHAP possesses non-trivial sampling stochasticity on 128-dimensional tensors, and that explainer jitter must be accounted for alongside model drift.

scientific_claim: Integrated Gradients proves that quantization attribution drift is an artifact of perturbation explainers.
calculation_or_experiment: Captum IG evaluated via FakeQuantization with Straight-Through Estimator (STE) on 50 flows: PTQ VPN rho = 0.9373, Top-5 IoU = 0.7376.
limitations_and_caveats: IG was evaluated on a continuous FakeQuantization surrogate with STE gradients, NOT the deployed discrete INT8 integer model (which has zero gradient).
final_wording_recommendation: Clarify that path-integral gradient methods integrate across continuous weight paths via STE, smoothing over discrete integer threshold flips that perturbation-based sampling exposes.

scientific_claim: Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) resolves attribution drift (IoU rises to 0.73).
source_artifact: Early 3-epoch developmental draft vs finalized 5-epoch QAT evaluation
calculation_or_experiment: On paired 30 VPN flows: PTQ Top-5 IoU is 0.3866, QAT Top-5 IoU is 0.3310 (a decrease of 0.0556). Paired Spearman rho is 0.3736 (PTQ) vs 0.3850 (QAT).
limitations_and_caveats: Initial 3-epoch claim of recovery was refuted by rigorous 5-epoch true INT8 evaluation. Cross-entropy task loss is blind to attribution geometry.
final_wording_recommendation: Embrace the authentic negative result: Standard task-loss QAT does not resolve attribution drift on VPN flows, demonstrating that drift is a deep structural consequence requiring attribution-regularized loss functions.

scientific_claim: Unverified INT8 edge deployment constitutes an automated operational security failure and direct regulatory non-compliance.
source_artifact: Threat modeling and regulatory analysis sections
calculation_or_experiment: Qualitative analysis of automated SOAR dynamic firewall rule generation and EU AI Act Art. 13 / GDPR Art. 22 transparency requirements.
limitations_and_caveats: No empirical test of a physical firewall was conducted. Coarse handshake/payload attention is conserved (~31.4% / ~68.6%), though fine-grained packet rankings drift.
final_wording_recommendation: Frame as an operational threat model and qualitative regulatory compliance risk index rather than an empirical security failure or judicial determination.
